*.defect_claim: The cited code has the defect the named lint rule describes.
premises: The cited line has the behaviour the named rule's message describes, in code that runs (not a test fixture, generated file or dead branch).
The behaviour is a defect in this context: a correct program would not keep it, rather than a style preference the codebase allows.

no-console.defect_claim: The cited line calls a console method in backend code, which CLAUDE.md forbids; the message belongs on the NestJS Logger.
premises: CLAUDE.md forbids console.* in backend code (apps, libs, platform/libs) and requires the NestJS Logger, whatever the project's own lint allows.
The cited line calls a method of the global console object, in code that runs (not a test fixture, a generated file, a string or a comment).

@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any.defect_claim: The cited line types a value as any in backend code, which switches the type checker off for that value; CLAUDE.md forbids it.
premises: CLAUDE.md forbids escaping the type system with any (`as any` is named FORBIDDEN: fix the type or write a generic), whatever the project's own lint allows.
The cited line is a TypeScript type position that names any (an annotation, an assertion or a type argument), in code that runs (not a test fixture, a generated file, a string or a comment).

aria-policy/no-double-type-assertion.defect_claim: The cited line asserts a value through unknown to another type in backend code, which switches the type checker off for that value; CLAUDE.md forbids it.
premises: CLAUDE.md forbids `as unknown as X` (fix the type or write a generic), whatever the project's own lint allows.
The cited line asserts an expression to unknown and then to another type, in code that runs (not a test fixture, a generated file, a string or a comment).
